content: What do people think of renaming docs#measurable_pi_lambda to Measurable.of_eval? This is the lemma that says that f : X -> Y -> Z is measurable if for every y : Y, x => f x y is measurable. I've always found this name out of place, especially the "lambda" part. Also I would take the opportunity to make f implicit in the lemma, I've always written it with an _.
I opened #42979, in which I also renamed docs#aemeasurable_pi_lambda to AEMeasurable.of_eval.

There are the classes ContinuousEvalConst that says that the map f ↦ f x is continuous for every x and ContinuousEval that says that the map (f, x) ↦ f x is jointly continuous. Would it make sense based on these that the lemma contains const in the name, since the lemma has a ∀ (a : δ) in the proposition?
can we also fix other similar lemmas, e.g. docs#monotone_lam
What a lam name :drum:
